content:
Want to use Signal on multiple devices at the same time? This encrypted communication service now makes it easier for users to use the app across iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, no longer limited to setting up an auxiliary device as an iPad.

When announcing the simultaneous rollout of Android linking support, Signal stated: "We have also expanded linked device support on iOS. In addition to the iPad support we have always offered, you can now link an iPhone to your Signal account."

When linking an additional iPhone, users can choose to transfer the complete message history, along with media files saved within the past 45 days.

Signal pointed out that the transfer process uses full end-to-end encryption, employing the same "link-and-sync" technology used for iPads and desktop devices (including the Signal Mac app).

This expanded support is particularly useful for users who use both a work and personal iPhone, and is also suitable for those who need to test multiple devices.

This update also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to the Apple Messages ecosystem, enabling seamless conversation syncing across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

The Signal iOS version 8.22 has begun rolling out gradually on the App Store. Signal previously also introduced a username feature, allowing users to establish contacts without sharing a phone number.
